items.item: The form is split into titled sections (personal, job and contract, bank and tax, emergency contact, documents) in a single column, with a visible label above every field and no placeholder-only labels
items.evidence: Five <section> blocks each with <h2 class="section-title">: 'Personal details', 'Job and contract', 'Bank and tax information', 'Emergency contact', 'Documents' (lines 100,193,323,382,426). Every input has a <label class="field-label" for=...> above it (e.g. 'First name', 'National ID / Passport number'); placeholders like 'e.g. Jane' are supplementary hints, not substitutes for labels. Layout is a single main column (max-w-3xl) with only closely-related pairs (first/last name, city/postal, start/end date) sharing a row.

items.item: Required fields are marked consistently, and optional fields are labelled as optional or left unmarked by a stated convention
items.evidence: Page states the convention 'p class="mb-6 text-sm text-slate-600">* Required' (line 89). Every required field's label ends with '*' (e.g. firstName line 104); optional fields such as preferredName, addressLine, city, alternatePhone, contactEmail, filingStatus, probationPeriodMonths carry no asterisk, consistent with the stated convention.

items.item: Field widths match their content: dates, postal codes and tax codes are narrow; inputs use the right types (email, tel, date)
items.evidence: dateOfBirth/startDate/endDate wrapped in 'w-40' containers (lines 122,243,248), postalCode in 'w-28' (line 167), taxId in 'w-48' (line 360) — all narrow vs. max-w-md/max-w-xl text fields. Correct input types: type="date" for date fields, type="email" for personalEmail/contactEmail, type="tel" for phone/contactPhone/alternatePhone (lines 124,146,153,245,250,406,412,418).

items.item: An option to save the form as a draft is offered, and saving a draft does not demand every required field
items.evidence: '<button type="button" id="draftBtn" class="btn btn-secondary">Save draft</button>' (line 530). Its click handler (line 846) only updates the status badge/toast and never calls validateAndShow/FIELDS validation, so an incomplete form can still be saved as a draft.

items.item: Save and Cancel stay reachable while scrolling (a sticky bar or equivalent), Save is a verb label and is not disabled before submitting

items.item: Fields validate on blur and on submit; with several errors a summary at the top links to each field and focus moves to the first invalid field
items.evidence: Text inputs validate on 'blur' and selects on 'change' (line 681); form submit handler (line 818) re-validates all FIELDS. renderErrorSummary() builds an anchor list ('a.href="#"+err.field.name') for each error once errors.length >= 3 (lines 696-729), and on submit focusField(errors[0].field.name) calls .focus() and scrollIntoView on the first invalid control (lines 649-653, 838-840).

items.item: Leaving the page with unsaved input triggers a warning
items.evidence: markDirty() registers a 'beforeunload' handler that calls e.preventDefault() (lines 656,665-670); Cancel and the 'Employees' breadcrumb link both route through attemptLeave(), which shows an in-page '<div id="leaveDialog" role="alertdialog">You have unsaved changes / Leave without saving?' confirmation when isDirty is true (lines 539-548, 860-869).

items.item: The document upload states accepted file types and the size limit, lists chosen files with a remove button, and is keyboard operable
items.evidence: 'Accepted formats: PDF, JPG, PNG, up to 10 MB.' (line 427). Each uploaded row shows the chosen filename/type/size (doc-meta, e.g. 'passport_scan.pdf · PDF · 1.2 MB', line 437) plus a '<button class="btn-link doc-remove">Remove</button>' (line 445/765). Uploads are triggered by real <button> elements calling fileInput.click() (lines 751, 462/515), so they respond to native keyboard activation (Enter/Space) despite the underlying <input type="file" class="hidden">.

items.item: Success is confirmed with a message that names the employee and is announced to assistive technology
items.evidence: doSave() builds the full name from firstName/lastName and calls showToast('Employee ' + name + ' submitted for approval.') (lines 811-812). The toast container is '<div id="toast" role="status" aria-live="polite">' (line 550), so it is announced to assistive technology.

notes: Header shows a generic role-initials avatar 'HR' for the signed-in user (user@example.com) rather than the actual person's initials, which reads as a templated placeholder rather than a bound user identity. Otherwise the screen is a clean, restrained enterprise form: no gradients/glass/emoji/uppercase tracked labels/rainbow badges/decorative charts were found, consistent with the audit's clean metrics (radii 4/6, no hard-stop gradients, no emoji-icon or uppercase-text violations). The sticky action bar appears mid-page in the stitched full-page screenshot; that is an artifact of how full-page capture freezes a sticky element at its last on-screen scroll position, not a real positioning bug — the bar is 'position: sticky; bottom: 0' inside the form and pins to the viewport bottom during actual scrolling.
